summary.title: Tstars-Tryon 1.0: Robust and Realistic Virtual Try-On for Diverse Fashion Items

details: Existing try-on and general image-editing models fail commercial requirements: robustness to in-the-wild user photos, fine-grained garment fidelity, multi-item/multi-reference outfit composition, and near real-time latency.

Tstars-Tryon 1.0: a 5B-parameter unified MMDiT virtual try-on system that reframes try-on as multi-reference image editing (no inpainting masks), jointly conditioning on up to 6 reference fashion items plus person and background control.

Full-stack recipe as the contribution: automated multi-item data engine, packing-based variable-resolution/variable-reference training infra, multi-stage pretrain -> SFT -> DiffusionNFT RL, prompt rewriter, and CFG+step distillation for low-latency serving.
Tstars-VTON Benchmark: 1780 unpaired real-world try-on samples with a VLM-based 4-dimension scoring protocol (identity, garment fidelity, background, physical/structural logic).
1780 paired samples, 5 garment + 3 accessory categories, 465 fine-grained sub-styles, 1-6 layered items per sample.

Three-stage pipeline: tag-guided retrieval from internet/e-commerce, VLM + human filtering and fine-grained tagging (11 model tag dims, 13 garment dims), face-swap anonymization against a licensed face database, then rule-based physically plausible layering pairing.
Statistics: 74.9% female / 25.1% male, 29.6% complex poses, >40% highly complex backgrounds.
Scores on 1-10 Likert scale via two separate VLM calls (garment-aware vs garment-agnostic); Overall = geometric mean to penalize weak links.
Unified MMDiT DiT of 5B params; native variable resolution and arbitrary number of reference images via data packing (replacing bucketing), with data + tensor parallelism.

Pretraining with task-/content-balanced data and progressive difficulty plus progressive resolution scaling; high-quality vertical-domain SFT; RL with group-level trajectory sampling, multi-dimensional reward and DiffusionNFT, yielding CFG-free inference.
Inference acceleration by CFG distillation plus step distillation; tailored prompt rewriter model for semantic guidance.
8 supported item categories: tops, pants, skirts, dresses, coats, shoes, bags, hats.
Academic try-on: CatVTON, Leffa, FitDiT, FastFit.
Open-source editors: QwenEdit-2511, FLUX.2-dev, FLUX.2-klein-9B, FireRed-Image-Edit-1.1.
Proprietary: GPT-Image-1.5, GPT-Image-2, Nano Banana Pro, Seedream5 lite (queried via API at high quality; some cases failed and were excluded).
Tstars-VTON Benchmark, single- and multi-garment splits (multi averages 5 references).
Academic zero-shot transfer: VITON-HD (2,032 test pairs) and DressCode (5,400 test pairs), unpaired setting with FID/KID; no VITON-HD or DressCode data in training.
Human GSB pairwise study vs Nano Banana Pro, Seedream5 lite, GPT-Image-2, broken down by number of reference garments.
Latency measured on an H200 GPU; closed-source timings estimated via API.

key_findings.finding: A 5B distilled try-on model surpasses leading proprietary general-purpose editors on a commercial-grade try-on benchmark while running one to two orders of magnitude faster.
key_findings.evidence: Single-garment Overall 9.372 vs Seedream5 lite 9.301, Nano Banana Pro 9.229, GPT-Image-2 9.200; multi-garment Overall 9.171 vs GPT-Image-2 9.111 and Seedream5 lite 8.914. Latency 3.92s single-garment and 6.74s multi-garment (avg 5 references) on H200, versus roughly 200s for QwenEdit-2511 and FLUX.2-dev.

key_findings.finding: General-purpose editing models collapse when moving from single- to multi-garment try-on, whereas the proposed system stays stable.
key_findings.evidence: FireRed-Image-Edit-1.1 drops from 8.863 (single) to 4.822 (multi) Overall and QwenEdit-2511 from 8.121 to 6.441, with failures attributed to garment omission, unresolved layering, and identity/structure breakdown; Tstars-Tryon drops only 9.372 to 9.171.

key_findings.finding: Human preference advantage grows monotonically with outfit complexity.
key_findings.evidence: GSB win rate vs Nano Banana Pro rises from 33.6% (1 garment) to 54.8% (5 garments); vs GPT-Image-2 from 36.4% to 50.0%; vs Seedream5 lite from 46.1% to 70.2%. Overall: 41.1% win / 41.6% tie / 17.3% loss vs Nano Banana Pro, 54.4% vs 9.0% against Seedream5 lite.

key_findings.finding: The model generalizes zero-shot to academic try-on benchmarks despite never training on them.
key_findings.evidence: Unpaired setting: VITON-HD FID 8.485 / KID 0.528 (best, vs FastFit 8.629 / 0.665); DressCode KID 0.458 (best) with FID 4.541 (second to FastFit's 4.397).
